अरे भइया! क्या आपने कभी किसी मालिक को अपने घर की कामवाली के प्यार में पड़ते देखा है? 🍿

SonyLIV पर 1 घंटे 52 मिनट की फिल्म Parivarik ManuRanjan स्ट्रीम हो रही है, जिसे Varun V Sharma ने डायरेक्ट किया है।

फिल्म में Pankaj Tripathi (Ranjan) को अपनी हाउसहेल्प Aditi Rao Hydari से प्यार हो जाता है, जो समाज के क्लास डिवाइड की सोच को चुनौती देता है।

Pankaj Tripathi की बेहतरीन एक्टिंग और Aditi Rao Hydari की सादगी इस फिल्म का सबसे बड़ा प्लस पॉइंट है। 🎬

हालांकि रिव्यू के मुताबिक, सेकंड हाफ में ढीली स्क्रिप्ट और सेफ ह्यूमर के कारण फिल्म अपने मेन मुद्दे से थोड़ा भटक जाती है। 💔

क्या आप Pankaj Tripathi की यह नई फिल्म देखने का प्लान बना रहे हैं? कमेंट्स में अपनी राय बताएं! 👇

ctx.summary:
In Pankaj Tripathi & Aditi Rao Hydari’s film, falling in love with a househelp isn’t a problem; not daring to resolve it with a spine is the problem - Parivarik ManuRanjan movie review! 
 The post  Parivarik ManuRanjan Movie Review: Pankaj Tripathi Dares To Fall In Love With His Househelp In A Spineless Film Ft. Aditi Rao Hydari!  appeared first on  Koimoi .
ctx.text: Parivarik ManuRanjan Movie Review Rating: Star Cast: Pankaj Tripathi, Aditi Rao Hydari, and a supporting cast playing the quintessential sanskaari family crowd. Director: Varun V Sharma Parivarik ManuRanjan Movie Review: Pankaj Tripathi & Aditi Rao Hydari’s Film Could Have Been So Daring! (Photo Credit: Sony LIV) What’s Good: Pankaj Tripathi’s effortless warmth, Aditi Rao Hydari’s quiet dignity, and a remarkably progressive core premise that dares to challenge deep-rooted Indian class conditioning. What’s Bad: A cowardly screenplay that chickens out in the second half, hiding behind safe, veiled humor instead of confronting the ugly social stigmas it initially sets out to dismantle. Loo Break: Anytime the film repeats its loop! Watch or Not?: Yes, it definitely is your regular, harmless, feel-good film! Language: Hindi Available On: SonyLIV Runtime: 1 hour and 52 Minutes User Rating: Have you ever heard of a man falling in love with his househelp? Or vice versa? We have heard many such stories being discussed in our living rooms, serving as the utmost gossip platters! So, what is so intriguing about these stories? It is the class divide! The basic societal structure that says that you cannot fall in love with your househelp! That is the basic norm of hierarchy! So, when one dares to do it, then it is against the rules of societal development, and hence it is the most celebrated whispered gossip! So when Pankaj Tripathi and Aditi Rao Hydari decided to attempt a househelp rom-com, the move looked daring! But does the film dare to address this societal stigma well enough? Does it finally resolve this so-called class divide? Does it deliver a powerful social message? Let us find out in our review! Parivarik ManuRanjan Movie Review: Pankaj Tripathi Plays A Man With Good Morals In A Spineless Film! (Photo Credit: YouTube) Parivarik ManuRanjan Movie Review: Script Analysis In a typical middle-class Indian household, hierarchy is an unspoken religion; everyone knows where they sit, who serves the tea, and which lines are never meant to be crossed. Parivarik ManuRanjan dares to disrupt this cozy hypocrisy right at the dining table! The film follows a gentle, middle-aged man ( Pankaj Tripathi ) living under the watchful eyes of his conventional family, who finds an unexpected, tender companionship with his househelp (Aditi Rao Hydari). What starts as shared silences, mutual respect, and quiet empathy slowly blossoms into genuine love. On paper, this is dynamite – a mature, unconventional romance that forces a parivarik audience to look into the mirror and confront their own class prejudice. Parivarik ManuRanjan Movie Review: Star Performance If Parivarik ManuRanjan still manages to tug at your heartstrings despite its cold feet, credit goes entirely to its two extraordinary leads. Pankaj Tripathi is, once again, the reason to watch. He is pure magic when playing men who carry quiet revolutions beneath their soft-spoken personalities. He doesn’t need big gestures: a raised eyebrow, a pause before a line, and a half-smile are enough. As Ranjan, he is vulnerable, funny, and believable, and he makes you root for this man even when the film doesn’t give him enough to fight for. Aditi Rao Hydari brings a lovely simplicity and a small-town honesty to her role. She looks gorgeous, as always, but more importantly, she gives the character dignity. The pairing may seem unusual on paper, but their chemistry is warm and easy. My only complaint is that the writing doesn’t give her enough of an inner life. Brijendra Kala, Sunita Rajwar, and the rest of the supporting cast do not add anything substantial to the film because the script never dares to fly!
